Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

malariafwd 0.1.0

The first release. malariafwd runs a forward, individual-based simulation of Plasmodium vivax transmission and genetics from R, and reads its recorded genealogy as ground truth: who infected whom, whether each recurrence is a relapse, a reinfection or a recrudescence, and how related any two parasite genomes are. It is a pre-release: the interface and the model may change before 1.0.0. It needs SLiM 5.2 or newer, and Python with tskit for the relatedness functions; check_setup() reports both.

What it contains

  • The model, in SLiM with tskit tree-sequence recording: day-by-day human-mosquito transmission with superinfection; a hypnozoite reservoir whose batches activate (relapse) or die; case management, radical cure, mass drug administration and recrudescence; four-strand meiosis in the mosquito on the 14 chromosomes of the PvP01 reference genome; importation, vector control, seasonality and resurgence. Everything beyond the core is off by default.
  • Running it: vivax_params(), with every parameter described in ?vivax_params and param_info(); run_sim(); run_grid(), for parallel sweeps that resume where they stopped.
  • An example run: example_run() returns a small run that ships with the package, so every function that reads a run can be tried without SLiM.
  • Ground truth: classify_cases(), episodes(), recurrences(), transmission_links(), classify_chain() and rc_by_origin(), with classify_travel() for what a travel-history rule concludes instead.
  • Relatedness: ibd_pairs() and ibd_segments() read identity-by-descent from the tree sequence; simulate_genotypes() and write_vcf() paint marker genotypes on the genealogy, with the truth behind every call; arg_tmrca() and arg_summary() describe the genealogy itself.
  • Summaries and plots: summarise_run(), force_of_infection(), relapse_fraction(), new_infection_diversity(), plot_diagnostics() and the other plot_*() functions.
  • Validation: the scripts in inst/validation, installed under system.file("validation", package = "malariafwd"), audit the event log, the host states, the tree sequence and the IBD against what the model must produce, and check that each parameter moves the outputs the way it should.

Before drawing conclusions

  • NU_HYPNOZOITE_BATCH = 3 is fitted to four calibration targets, ranges taken from published P. vivax studies, at moderate transmission (inst/validation/calibrate_nu.R repeats the fit). The other defaults are an illustrative preview, 40 hosts for a year, not a calibrated setting.
  • Imported parasites are unrelated to local ones, so an import-detection result is an upper bound.
  • No study has measured how many genotypes a natural bite delivers. At the defaults (LAMBDA_OOCYSTS and LAMBDA_SPOROZOITES of 2) a bite can co-transmit several: sweep them.
  • There are no within-host densities, no post-treatment prophylaxis and no spatial structure.

The README lists these limitations with the others. The model description gives the model in full, with its assumptions and its validation, and the design decisions give the reasons for each modelling choice.

In development

  • Each hypnozoite genotyped independently of the bite’s primary infections, so that a relapse can differ from the primary of its own bite. This will change every default run.
  • A structured source population for imports, so that imported parasites carry real ancestry and can be related to one another.
  • Post-treatment prophylaxis: protection that wanes after each course.
  • More extensive calibration of the treatment and recurrence machinery, including a chloroquine-resistant setting, in which recrudescence is material rather than negligible.

The roadmap lists every planned extension with its motivation.
